ranking.note: Raised to P2: fixes transient censorship of 1p1c package parents, a pinning/fee-bumping concern this category ranks first, on par with the other acceptance-correctness fixes
Lowered to P3: relay-policy expansion revisiting closed #27926 with no cited downstream demand, so its benefit is more speculative than the P2 correctness/eviction fixes
Lowered to P4: two narrow reject-reason assertions for already-enforced Taproot rules, no behaviour change and no concrete regression history
Lowered to P4: explicitly not intended for merge, vendors experimental libsecp modules, and its mempool-standardness element is incidental to a consensus-level proposal

inconsistencies: #36328, #35286 and #36608 all touch package acceptance/submitpackage: review #36328 first (it changes the acceptance result semantics for trimmed package transactions), then #35286 (test-only package validation built on those semantics), then #36608's 1p1c submitpackage additions.

#36608 claims to fix a fee-sum overflow during package handling with extreme prioritisetransaction deltas, which is the same defect #36367 addresses directly; #36367 is the focused fix and should be reviewed and merged first to avoid duplicated or conflicting clamping logic.

#36841 adds regression coverage for CVE-2025-62861 already fixed in merged #33504, so its value is purely in the new Assume invariants and fuzz reorg path, not in fixing live behaviour; #35026 touches the same removeForReorg/MaybeUpdateMempoolForReorg area and will likely interact with those invariants.
#36816 is a prerequisite-style guard for the multiprocess IPC chain interface (#29409); its value is contingent on that chain landing, which is why it sits low in P3 despite being a correctness fix.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: four PRs fixing concrete acceptance/eviction/overflow misbehaviour (P2), a middle group of features, policy proposals and targeted test coverage with real but deferrable value (P3), and two marginal items. No PR here is category-critical: none is an unfixed remote DoS or pinning vector, and the one CVE-related item is after-the-fact regression coverage.
